debian_original_candidate.decision: Do not represent this inspected candidate as OpenPGP-verified.
debian_original_candidate.format: Plain text SHA512 checksum list, not clear-signed. Inspected latest and dated indexes advertise SHA512SUMS only; SHA512SUMS.sign HEAD was404 in initial readiness. No conclusion about all Debian image publication channels.

recommended_alternate.key_authority: Official https://ubuntu.com/docs/public-images/public-images-how-to/verify-image-checksum/ publishes this full fingerprint as Ubuntu image signing key; retrieved over inherited TLS/CA. No separate out-of-band Web-of-Trust is claimed.
recommended_alternate.qualification: Only signed expected image hash, official metadata, and HEAD length are verified. Image body digest, bootability under TCG, guest identity generation, application dependency transfer, and runtime execution remain untested. Alternate distro/image choice needs architectural confirmation before implementation.
recommended_alternate.signature_format: Detached OpenPGP binary signature (RSA4096/SHA512) over plaintext SHA256SUMS.
recommended_alternate.verification: /usr/bin/sqv --keyring ubuntu-cloud-pubkey.asc ubuntu-dated-SHA256SUMS.gpg ubuntu-dated-SHA256SUMS exited0 and returned the expected full fingerprint.

proposed_boot_only_controls_not_run: Two overlapping real QEMU TCG processes, each1vCPU/512MiB, distinct exact guest kernel boot_id and machine-id plus guest hostname; same physical host explicitly recorded.
Read-only common signed OS base, independent bounded qcow2 overlays and private UEFI vars; no9p,virtiofs,TAP/TUN,KVM or shared writable guest filesystem.

Cloud-init obtains only owned bounded HTTP metadata/artifacts over an explicitly restricted user-mode route; no guest package update or general Internet egress. Controller binds loopback only; allow only exact owned metadata/artifact paths and small body sizes. Actual slirp/NoCloud behavior must be verified, not inferred from a command line.
Round-trip two different small checksum-bound artifacts over that HTTP path, returning per-guest identity and payload digest; no Prefect runtime/dependency installation or native application credit.

Pin host QEMU pid/startticks/pidfd, deliberately stop one guest while the other remains live, wait/reap exact host process and retain stop receipt; no timeout-as-death. Clean up both guests and only owned writable files.

proposed_boot_only_resource_envelope.admission_rule: Immediately before any binary allocation or guest start, fresh baseline memory.current + remaining allocated-file cap + all configured guest RAM + explicit QEMU/controller overhead must be strictly below14GiB; filesystem free must cover the physical allocated cap and margin. Include already-running guests and all other workloads. Re-evaluate before guest2; suspend progress/stop owned probe if the guard cannot be maintained. Arithmetic at this snapshot is not a future reservation.
proposed_boot_only_resource_envelope.qualification: /tmp is tmpfs. The<=1GiB file budget adds to guest RAM. At this observation the2x512MiB proposal fits the conservative arithmetic narrowly; actual QEMU overhead,512MiB Ubuntu cloud-init boot, application-free artifact delivery, and the bounded watcher remain untested. A two1GiB native application profile is a separate later resource decision.
watcher_plan: Start a bounded controller before QEMU. Record exact pid, /proc startticks, pidfd, private disk paths and own children as soon as Popen succeeds; never discard a handle on initialization error.

Monitor cgroup memory.current, allocated st_blocks*512 for unique owned inodes, individual file sizes, filesystem available bytes, controller/guest status and monotonic deadline. Keep an explicit reserve and stop early enough for sampling/signal latency; do not promise zero overshoot.

Set each QEMU RLIMIT_FSIZE256MiB for writable overlay files and cap/rotate or stream logs to bounded controller files. Preserve private UEFI vars per guest. Guest disk-full/file-limit must fail the probe, never consume unbounded tmpfs.

If a budget/deadline guard trips, stop only exact owned QEMU processes through pidfd, then wait/reap and verify recorded identity gone. Keep ownership and resources on an unknown wait/kill ACK, retry cleanup; never treat timeout, guest disconnect or lease expiry as death.

Remove only the owned overlays/firmware-vars/artifacts after exact guest exits are proven. Keep immutable receipts and failure logs within their stated cap. Never prune Docker, touch old soak/PG17, drop host caches or change services to make room.
